graph_degree.reason: The native score fits no source-specific parameter, but it can still leak evaluated-source observability or derivative edges unless removal is exhaustive.

graph_source_count.reason: The native score fits no parameters and uses only remaining source families, but aliases and derived releases must collapse before counting.

regularized_linear_evidence.reason: It requires enough development source families with explicit supported and tested-negative candidates to create pseudo-held-source training examples and nested source plus LD/gene-block folds. That feasibility is currently unresolved.

held_source_feasibility.seal_status: No current source is sealed. Even a leakage-safe source-removal result is exposed retrospective development evidence and cannot earn a champion.

known_leakage_routes: Building the candidate universe, gene or locus roster, label denominator, edge ontology, source taxonomy, feature lexicon, or status thresholds from the evaluated source.

Retaining evaluated-source aliases, inverse edges, source nodes, provenance, observability, coverage, tested status, missingness, deterministic derivatives, aggregates, paths, degrees, source counts, or normalization.
Removing a source after degree, counts, features, embeddings, negatives, normalization, or candidate rows have already been computed.
Retaining any edge incident to an outer-held locus before graph construction, feature aggregation, training-example creation, or calibration.
Splitting variants within ancestry-aware native-build LD blocks, one locus, one gene block, source aliases, technical releases, or graph derivatives across roles.
Treating an absent edge, untested candidate, unobservable assay, not-applicable source, unavailable permission, failed join, discordant result, or indeterminate result as a tested negative.
Counting accessions, publications, technical replicates, alleles, barcodes, cells, guides, or derivative tables from one experiment as independent sources.
Pooling continuous colocalization, MPRA, perturbation, distance, and other assay values before retaining source, metric, unit, direction, and missing state.
Using evaluated-source prevalence, observability, eligibility, score distribution, or labels to calibrate degree, counts, or linear probabilities.
Using entity IDs or transductive graph embeddings in regularized_linear_evidence so held candidates inherit outcome-coded identity.
Using the provisional Gene Catalog or frozen 117 programs as model-selection targets or pseudo-sealed labels.

observability_and_bias_disposition.graph_degree: A direct graph-popularity and study-intensity guard. Report in/out composition, edge-type concentration, remaining-source observability strata, and correlation with all graph model scores.
observability_and_bias_disposition.graph_source_count: A source-breadth guard. Report alias collapse, per-source contributions, source concentration, and remaining-source applicability strata.
observability_and_bias_disposition.regularized_linear_evidence: Can learn observability and source-size bias. Report raw-unit feature definitions, state coefficients, source-held calibration, coefficient stability, and performance after removal of explicit observability features.
observability_and_bias_disposition.held_observability: Evaluator-only for all three. It may stratify terminal scoring under a frozen evaluator but cannot be a feature, calibration input, or model-selection aid.
observability_and_bias_disposition.zero: Numeric zero requires an observed applicable remaining graph. No applicable or observable evidence is structurally_missing.

replication_and_uncertainty_disposition.unit: independent native-build LD locus; gene-block dependence is additionally retained
replication_and_uncertainty_disposition.bootstrap: 10000 paired two-way LD-block and gene-block replicates with nested graph rows preserved
replication_and_uncertainty_disposition.multiplicity: BH q<0.05 within the secondary typed-evidence-graph source and endpoint family

calibration_disposition.graph_degree: No native probability. Brier is ineligible until a source-blind cross-fitted one-dimensional calibrator has its own immutable fit receipt.
calibration_disposition.graph_source_count: No native probability. Brier is ineligible until a source-blind cross-fitted one-dimensional calibrator has its own immutable fit receipt.
calibration_disposition.regularized_linear_evidence: Native sigmoid probability reflects the frozen equal-source and equal-block development mixture. Report Brier without held-source recalibration and state that its prevalence target is the development mixture.
calibration_disposition.prohibition: No evaluated-source prevalence, eligibility, observability, threshold, or outcome enters calibration.

license_and_release_disposition.graph_and_data: Every graph input, source ID, evidence row, aggregate, coefficient, and prediction remains subject to its source terms and the aggregate-only Resource policy.
license_and_release_disposition.release: No implementation or fitted artifact may be described as reproducible or releasable until immutable source, runtime, graph, and output receipts exist.

remaining_blockers: Promote the corrected 50-study COLOC release and freeze one immutable graph snapshot, evidence ontology, edge direction and type roster, source-family aliases, evidence-unit identity, statuses, observability, native-build LD blocks, loci, gene blocks, and source-independent candidate universe.
Resolve whether enough independent development source families have explicit tested-negative denominators to fit and select regularized_linear_evidence without row-level pseudoreplication.
Implement exhaustive held-source and held-block removal before any graph or feature derivative and prove the removal receipt has no residual source path.
Implement exact canonical degree, supporting-source count, and cross-source ridge-logistic formulas with deterministic ties, the frozen regularization grid, and bounded coefficient artifacts.
Register source-blind cross-fitted calibrators for degree and source count if Brier is retained; do not calibrate to the evaluated source.

Pass approved CPU-SLURM synthetic fixtures for aliases, inverse edges, technical replicates, edge direction, held-source-only candidates, missing versus zero, explicit negatives, source removal, LD/gene grouping, row-order invariance, coefficient reproduction, and output hashes.
Keep all findings development-only and use candidate-prioritization language until a wholly sealed graph source is prospectively registered and powered.
